To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the Hessian of a nonlinear optimization problem are useful for analyzing and understanding the behavior of the problem, (b) the eigenvalue distribution of the Hessian is closely related to the distribution of the objective function, (c) the eigenvector distribution is related to the structure of the problem, and (d) the eigenspectrum is closely related to both the objective function and the structure of the optimization problem

(1) the Hessian matrix of the loss functions for the three nonlinear models considered in this paper is not positive semi-definite, (2) the eigenvalues of the Hessian matrices are all real, (3) the Hessian matrices have at least one negative eigenvalue, (4) the Hessian eigenvalues are all negative, except for one, and that eigenvalue is zero, and (5) the Hessian is singular, and therefore not invertible.
The eigenvalues of the Hessian matrix are the same as the eigenvalues of the matrix.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following three problems.
the following questions: (1) How do we construct the Hessian matrix of an optimization problem? (2) What can be learned about the problem structure from its Hessian?
the following questions: (1) How can we compute the eigenspectra of Hessians of nonlinear models?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no single best algorithm for solving a general nonlinear programming problem, and that a number of algorithms may be needed for solving a particular problem.
the Hessian is a useful tool in optimization, but it is not the only tool, and it is not necessarily the most important one.
the eigenvalues of the Hessian are a good indicator of the curvature of the objective function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the eigenspectrum of the Hessian matrix of the objective function is a powerful tool for analyzing the local behavior of the objective function.

we have shown that the Hessian matrix of a nonlinear model is a very useful tool for analyzing a model, and that it can be used in several ways to obtain information on the structure of the model and its behavior.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Hessian spectrum of a realistic model is much more complicated than the spectrum of a model that has been artificially simplified to be convex.
the Hessian matrix of a nonlinear model can be computed in an efficient manner, and that this can be done in a variety of ways depending on the specific application at hand.
the Hessian of a nonconvex problem can be more informative than one might expect, even when the problem itself is nonconvex.
